findings.description: The command leg refuses dangerous git flags by argument prefix. That check misses a grouped short option (`git grep -nO<prog> x` hides `-O`) and an abbreviated long option (`--outp=`, `--ext-d`, `--textc`), and the slice 1 tests list only the literal spellings.
findings.old: Any argument starting `-O`, `--open-files-in-pager`, `--output`, `--ext-diff`, `--textconv`, `--exec-path` or `--git-dir`, and a git-level `-c` before the subcommand, is refused (`git grep -c`, the count flag, stays allowed).
options: Replace the prefix deny-list with a positive per-subcommand option allow-list (each permitted flag spelled in full, grouped short options split and each letter checked, any unlisted `-`/`--` token refused). Add RED cases for `git grep -nOcalc x`, `git log --outp=f`, `git diff --stat --ext-d` and `git show --textc`.

Alternative: keep the deny-list but force safe execution, running with `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `-c core.pager=cat`, `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv` injected by the checker; wins if a positive allow-list proves too narrow for the claims round 1 and round 2 actually cite.
findings.rationale: KFM #50, 'Allow path judged only at segment heads' (`archive/feedback_guard_denial_of_justified_work_fix_the_guard.md`), matches this shape: the allow path checks token heads, and its proof lists only the allowed and literal shapes. The checked agent authors the command, so a bypass runs a program of its choosing inside the verifier. Rung: pattern. The claim rests on git parse-options behavior (grouped short options, unique-prefix long options); it has not been run here.

findings.description: The merge must-allow case rests on two unchecked premises. First, `_commit_scope.authored_paths` drops incoming paths after the merge is committed. Second, adding `--not --remotes` to the shared `owed_range` leaves `cmd_owed`'s output unchanged.
options: Recommended: drop `authored_paths` from this case. Rely on `--cc` (which `cmd_owed` already passes, so a merge commit lists only files that differ from every parent) plus `--not --remotes`, applied as a guard-only parameter of `owed_range`. Restate slice 1's unchanged-output test for `cmd_owed`'s current arguments.
Alternative: apply `--not --remotes` to `cmd_owed` too, and change slice 1's test to expect the narrowed output; wins if the owner wants `owed` and the guard to agree on every range.
findings.rationale: Shape 2/assumed mechanism. Read at _commit_scope.py:88-100: `authored_paths` acts only while MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD or REVERT_HEAD exists, and returns every path otherwise, so at push time it drops nothing. `cmd_owed` (review_ledger.py:2101-2105) uses `@{u}..HEAD` with no `--not --remotes`, so factoring the flag into the shared function contradicts slice 1's assertion that `owed` output stays unchanged for its current arguments. Rung: read.

evidence.quote: Without an operation in progress every path is this commit's own, so an ordinary commit is judged exactly as before.
